notes.summary: Primary Bedford–Taylor evidence: bounded local closed products, decreasing convergence, CLN bounds and pluripolar capacity zero; normalization is transported to D=i∂∂̄/(2π).
notes.detailedSummary: The retrieved primary paper supplies the local closed-product tools used below. No global theorem for mixed products with nonclosed Hermitian backgrounds is invoked. Its operator is 4πD, so k-fold closed products scale by (4π)^k. Source retrieval succeeded through the browser connector, while direct local downloads were denied.
notes.text:
Primary evidence and scope. In [Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf), the operator on printed p. 1 is 2i∂∂̄, hence 4π times our D. Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2, printed p. 4, give decreasing convergence and symmetric multilinearity for locally bounded psh functions and CLOSED local products. Theorem 2.10, printed p. 10, bounds their masses on compact subsets of a coordinate domain by sup norms. Theorem 6.9, printed p. 25, identifies pluripolar sets with zero outer capacity in a strongly pseudoconvex domain. We use coordinate balls, which meet that hypothesis.

A bounded psh function b on a ball can be shifted and divided by its oscillation to lie in [0,1]. Thus (Db)^n(E) is bounded by a constant times the local capacity of E. The zero-capacity assertion implies that this measure vanishes on locally pluripolar Borel sets. The same conclusion for (Db)^l∧β^(n-l), β=D|z|², follows by taking the positive term in the expansion of (D(b+|z|²))^n. Localization to smaller balls handles locally bounded functions and locally pluripolar sets. Positive rescaling of the operator preserves these zero sets.

Evidence files are sources/web_find.json and sources/direct_primary_crosschecks.json. Retrieve the exact URL above with the browser open operation, and find “Theorem 2.1”, “2.10” and “6.9”; sources/requests.json records rerun inputs. Direct urllib retrieval attempts and their errors are in sources/retrieval.json. These are primary theorem inputs, not new proofs of Bedford–Taylor theory.

notes.summary: Kołodziej–Nguyen Definition 1.1/Theorem 1.3 has the needed Hermitian Hölder-subsolution hypothesis and exact scaled conclusion, without lower/upper mass assumptions.
notes.detailedSummary: For positive finite Radon μ dominated by the Monge–Ampère measure of a global Hölder ω-psh function up to a constant, the published theorem gives a Hölder ω-psh solution with some c>0. It includes singular Borel data; no smooth-volume density or positive lower density is a hypothesis. Numerical operator conventions are handled by exact rescaling. A measurable-density convergence shortcut in its proof is diagnosed separately in n9.
notes.text:
Primary application input. [Kołodziej–Nguyen, AIF 68 (2018), 2951–2964](https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.3232.pdf), Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.3, printed p. 2952, concern a compact Hermitian (X,ω). For a positive Radon measure μ with 0<μ(X)<∞, the hypothesis is μ≤C₀(ω+ddᶜv)^n for some global Hölder continuous ω-psh v and C₀>0. The conclusion is an actual Hölder continuous ω-psh φ and c>0 satisfying (ω+ddᶜφ)^n=cμ. Neither v₋>0 nor v₊<∞ appears as an additional hypothesis. A density relative to smooth volume, or a positive lower bound for a density, is not required.

Convention transport, proved algebraically. Write the source operator as D_s=τD, τ>0. Apply its theorem with ω_s=τh, unchanged potentials, and μ_s=τ^nν. Then ω_s+D_s v=τ(h+Dv); consequently both domination and the exact equation divide by τ^n. This leaves φ and c unchanged. This argument avoids assigning a numerical convention not stated in the retrieved KN passages. It also preserves Hölder regularity and canonical quasi-psh representatives. Subtracting sup_X φ does not change the homogeneous equation.

The result is used as a published primary theorem, with its application checked below; it is not a premise granted by the question. The fixed-Borel-density weak-convergence step visible at printed p. 2958 cannot by itself justify the singular-data passage. See n9 for an explicit failure of that shortcut and a valid density-diagonal construction.

Evidence is in sources/web_find.json, sources/primary_setup.json and sources/kn_compactness_and_regularity.json. Rerun browser open at the URL above and printed pp. 2952 and 2958; source operation inputs are recorded in sources/requests.json.

notes.summary: ALS 2511.02339v1 Theorem 5.1 gives the exact bounded exponential equation for bounded densities against bounded-potential MA, with a bounded-rooftop convergence alternative.
notes.detailedSummary: The exact PDF theorem assumes a smooth semipositive big θ, bounded genuine θ-psh ψ and a bounded nonnegative measurable multiplier producing a nonzero measure; λ>0. It concludes bounded existence and uniqueness. Lemma 4.3 permits a rooftop equivalent to the reference instead of v₋>0. The PDF version, not the inconsistent-date HTML rendering, is the evidence used.
notes.text:
Primary application input. [Alehyane–Lu–Salouf, arXiv:2511.02339v1 PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1), Section 2, printed p. 5, fixes a compact Hermitian manifold and smooth semipositive big θ. Theorem 5.1, printed p. 20, assumes μ=f(θ+ddᶜψ)^n, ψ bounded θ-psh, f bounded nonnegative, μ(X)>0, and λ>0. It concludes a unique bounded θ-psh u solving (θ+ddᶜu)^n=e^(λu)μ. Its proof approximates f in L¹ of the reference Monge–Ampère measure, not of smooth volume.

Lemma 4.3, printed p. 19, requires L¹ convergence, uniformly finite masses, the rooftop Pθ(inf u_j) in the relative class, and ∫|e^(u_j)-e^u|MAθ(u_j)→0. Its extra alternative is rooftop equivalence to the reference OR v₋(θ)>0. Lemma 2.6, printed p. 7, supplies L¹ convergence against a fixed non-pluripolar Radon measure for uniformly bounded sequences. There is no blanket BMP hypothesis in Theorem 5.1.

Here θ=h is semipositive and genuinely big: h+D0=h dominates h. For a uniformly bounded sequence the rooftop is bounded between a constant and a uniform upper bound, so the bounded-reference alternative applies. This distinction is checked in the actual application n8.

Numerical conventions cause no loss: for D_s=τD, take θ_s=τh, ambient Hermitian form τh, μ_s=τ^nν and the same potential and λ. The exact source equation divides by τ^n and becomes precisely our equation.

Evidence files: sources/primary_setup.json, sources/als_details.json and sources/gl_and_als_limits.json. Rerun browser open at the exact PDF URL, printed pp. 5, 7, 19–22. The HTML endpoint labelled v1 displayed a different date from the PDF; it is not used as an additional mathematical premise. This note invokes the preprint theorem as external mathematical evidence, not as a newly proved result.

notes.summary: Published bounded domination needs individual noncollapse, not v₋>0; every smooth positive Hermitian h meets its torsion bounds, giving exponential uniqueness.
notes.detailedSummary: Guedj–Lu Corollary 1.6 and Proposition 2.8 apply to arbitrary Hermitian forms: their noncollapsing condition excludes a single bounded zero-mass potential, while uniform noncollapse is the stronger v₋>0 condition. For bounded exponential solutions, applying Proposition 2.8 on shifted strict-order sets proves pointwise uniqueness. Their ddᶜ is 2πD.
notes.text:
Indispensable published domination evidence. [Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 2, Algebraic Geometry 9 (2022), 688–713](https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2022-6/2022-6-021.pdf), printed p. 689, uses dᶜ=(∂-∂̄)/(2i), so ddᶜ=i∂∂̄=2πD. Definition 1.4 and Corollary 1.6 say that the derivative bounds (B) imply noncollapse: every bounded ω-psh potential has positive mass. This is distinct from their uniform noncollapse v₋(ω)>0. Proposition 2.8, printed p. 698, says that for such ω, bounded ω-psh x,y and 0≤a<1, MAω(x)≤a MAω(y) on {x<y} imply x≥y. Corollary 2.9 states the associated exponential order principle.

Check for h. Smoothness, strict positivity and compactness give finite operator norms for Dh relative to h² and dh∧dᶜh relative to h³. Thus a finite B satisfies the two-sided bounds (B); in dimensions where a form degree exceeds n that form is zero. Transport to ω_s=2πh proves that h is noncollapsing in the individual sense. This does not infer a positive infimum over all bounded potentials.

Proof of the uniqueness implication used later. Suppose bounded genuine x,y satisfy MA_h(x)=e^(λx)ν and MA_h(y)=e^(λy)ν. For every δ>0, on {x<y-δ},
MA_h(x)≤e^(-λδ)MA_h(y-δ).
The coefficient is strictly less than one. The proposition gives x≥y-δ globally. Let δ↓0 and exchange x,y. Then x=y at every canonical point, including points outside the support of ν. No additive-constant quotient is used.

Evidence files are sources/direct_primary_crosschecks.json, sources/compactness_crosschecks.json and sources/gl_and_als_limits.json. Rerun browser open at the link above, printed pp. 689, 694 and 698–699. No global nonclosed mixed-product multilinearity result from this source is used.

notes.summary: Local proof: all bounded Hermitian products have finite corrected masses; clipped-log sphere products have exact unit normalization for D.
notes.detailedSummary: A local closed-potential expansion constructs the full smooth-background corrected product, verifies positivity by convolution, and gives finite masses without BMP. For radial f(log|z|²), the top product is d(f′^n) in the radial variable. All lower products are explicit, and truncating the radial function at shrinking radii rules out an overlooked residual current at the origin.
notes.text:
Local corrected products. Put β=D|z|² on a coordinate ball V and let K⊂⊂V. For a bounded genuine h-psh b choose T>0 with Tβ≥h on V. Then q=b+T|z|² is bounded psh. Define, locally,
MA_h(b)=Σ_{l=0}^n binom(n,l)(Dq)^l∧(h-Tβ)^(n-l).                 (1)
Every term is a finite signed measure on K: the smooth factor has norm bounded by Cβ^(n-l), and the closed positive current (Dq)^l has finite β-trace mass by n1. The analogous formula defines every lower power.

Here is also the positivity and consistency check, without a global nonclosed mixed-product theorem. Regularize q by radial nonnegative convolution q_ε decreasing to its canonical value on smaller balls. Let b_ε=q_ε-T|z|². Convolving the positive current h+Db gives h+Db_ε≥-η_εβ, where η_ε↓0 bounds the modulus of continuity of the smooth coefficients of h. Hence b_ε+η_ε|z|² has positive h-Hessian. Its smooth powers are positive and expand as in (1), with q_ε+η_ε|z|² decreasing to q. Closed Bedford–Taylor convergence proves that these powers converge to (1). Applying the same smooth algebra with two choices of T proves independence of T. Coordinate changes and restrictions agree by locality of closed products. Thus these local definitions patch.

The measures in (1) vanish on locally pluripolar sets: each absolute variation is dominated locally by a constant times the trace of (Dq)^l, whose zero-set property follows from n1. A finite coordinate cover and a partition of unity show MA_h(b)(X)<∞ for this ACTUAL bounded b. This argument supplies bounds for any family with a fixed oscillation bound, but does not take a supremum over all bounded potentials. Since b has no poles, its extended non-pluripolar product is exactly (1).

Radial normalization. Set s=log|z|² on the punctured ball, L=Ds and Q=ds∧dᶜs, with dᶜ=i(∂̄-∂)/(4π). Then Q≥0, Q²=0, L≥0, L^n=0 and
D f(s)=f′L+f″Q,
(D f(s))^l=(f′)^l L^l+l(f′)^(l-1)f″ Q∧L^(l-1).                (2)
For smooth convex increasing f, its complex Hessian has n-1 eigenvalues f′/r² and one eigenvalue f″/r². With Euclidean dV,
(D f(s))^n=(n!/π^n)(f′)^(n-1)f″ r^(-2n)dV.
The sphere area is 2π^n r^(2n-1)/(n-1)!; integrating the angular variable gives
2n(f′)^(n-1)f″ dr/r=d((f′)^n).                               (3)
The angular probability is normalized Euclidean surface measure. Smooth convex regularizations of max(s,s_j) decrease to it; (3) therefore proves
(D max(log|z|²,log r_j²))^n=σ_j.
In particular max(log|z|,log r_j) would instead give 2^(-n)σ_j. The factor cannot be dropped.

All lower radial products. If f′=c(s) is constant between the s_j and jumps from B_j to C_j at s_j, (2) gives on the punctured ball
(D f(s))^l=c(s)^l L^l+
 Σ_j(C_j^l-B_j^l)δ(s-s_j)Q∧L^(l-1),  1≤l≤n.                (4)
The first term is an ordinary locally integrable form away from 0, and δ(s-s_j) is the hypersurface distribution in the radial variable. This identity follows by convex smoothing of each jump, because l c^(l-1)dc=d(c^l). It is a local closed-product computation. Moreover
δ(s-s_j)Q∧L^(n-1)=σ_j,
∫δ(s-s_j)Q∧L^(l-1)∧β^(n-l)=r_j^(2(n-l)).                  (5)
Indeed β=r²(L+Q), so after wedging Q only its L factors survive.

For the f used in n6, c(r)≤C√r and C_j≤C√r_j. For l<n, the trace of the continuous term in (4) is
(n-l)c(r)^l r^(2(n-l))ds,
integrable at 0 because 2(n-l)+l/2>0. The spherical trace series converges by the same exponent. To exclude an uncomputed origin term, use f_N(r)=max(f(r),f(r_N)). These are bounded psh decreasing to f, constant for r≤r_N. Their only replacement innermost spherical coefficient is C_N^l, with trace mass C_N^l r_N^(2(n-l))→0, including l=n. Decreasing convergence from n1 establishes (4) across 0 with no additional current there. This also proves absence of an atom in the top product directly.

Symbolic evidence, not an analytic certificate: checks/verify_formulas.py gives radial density 2n fp^(n-1)fpp/r, normalization residual 0, sphere-mass ratio 1 in n6, and origin exponent n/2>0. Rerun from the workspace with python checks/verify_formulas.py; its input/domain is checks/input.json and output is checks/formulas_output.json. Environment versions are Python 3.12.14 and SymPy 1.14.0. The mathematical arguments above are independent of execution success.

notes.summary: A–B proved for every h: ρ is singular non-pluripolar, and an explicit strict h-psh C^(0,1/2) potential has finite positive mass and dominates kρ.
notes.detailedSummary: Take a_j=√r_j and the uniformly convergent radial series F=Σa_j max(log|z|²,log r_j²). Its complete local top product is exactly A^nρ, A=Σa_j. The cutoff Hessians have a single uniform negative bound on a fixed annulus. Scaling by ε=[2(1+AL)]^(-1) and subtracting the supremum gives a genuine canonical strict potential uρ and k=(εA)^n. Continuity and explicit lower-product traces handle accumulation at p; no weak-limit preservation of non-pluripolarity or BMP is used.
notes.text:
Notation and actual formula. Write q₀=2^(-1/2), a_j=√r_j=√r₀ q₀^j, and
A=Σ_{j≥1}a_j=√r₀/(√2-1),
S_n=Σ_{j≥1}a_j^n=r₀^(n/2)2^(-n/2)/(1-2^(-n/2)).
On the supplied coordinate ball define
F(z)=Σ_{j≥1}a_j max(log|z|²,log r_j²),                       (6)
with the actual value F(0)=Σ a_j log r_j². Every term is bounded on a fixed relatively compact ball by a constant times 1+j, and Σ(1+j)a_j<∞. Thus (6) converges uniformly, including at 0, and is a finite continuous psh function. Extend G=χF by zero to X. Since χ has compact support inside the chart, this extension has no boundary discontinuity.

Uniform Hessian bound. Choose a radius R_* with r₁<R_* such that χ=1 on a neighborhood of the closed ball B_{R_*}; choose a larger compact coordinate ball containing supp χ. On its annular part r≥R_*, all clipped logarithms equal log r². Put
L_h=max(0, sup_{r≥R_*} sup_{ξ≠0} [-D(χ log|z|²)(ξ,Jξ)/h(ξ,Jξ)]),             (7)
where the supremum is taken on that fixed compact annulus and the expression is zero outside supp χ. This is an explicit finite nonnegative constant determined by the supplied h, chart and χ. Inside B_{R_*}, D(χ max(log r²,log r_j²))≥0. Outside it, this Hessian is exactly D(χ log r²). Therefore EACH cutoff summand has D≥-L_h h, uniformly in j. Summing uniformly, or testing distributions and passing to the limit, gives DG≥-A L_h h.

Set
ε=1/[2(1+A L_h)],     u_ρ=εG-sup_X(εG),     k=(εA)^n>0.     (8)
Then h+Du_ρ≥(1-εA L_h)h≥h/2. These are actual global functions and distributions, not almost-everywhere versions or envelopes. Local addition of a sufficiently large smooth quadratic turns u_ρ into a continuous psh function, so it is a genuine canonical quasi-psh representative. It has no poles and sup_X u_ρ=0.

Actual Hölder estimate. Between consecutive radii,
F′(r)=2c(r)/r,  c(r)=Σ_{r_j<r}a_j.
The largest active radius is less than r, hence c(r)≤√r/(1-q₀). This also holds for r≥r₁. Consequently, for 0≤s≤r,
0≤F(r)-F(s)≤[4/(1-q₀)](√r-√s)≤[4/(1-q₀)]√(r-s).
Continuity gives the inequality at s=0. Since ||z|-|w||≤|z-w|, it proves the Euclidean C^(0,1/2) estimate. For χF, use
|χ(z)F(z)-χ(w)F(w)|≤||χ||∞|F(z)-F(w)|+||F||∞ Lip(χ)|z-w|.
The second term is also bounded by a constant times |z-w|^(1/2) on the compact coordinate region. It patches through χ=0, and coordinate distances are comparable to any fixed Hermitian distance on smaller charts. A finite cover, plus boundedness for pairs at a fixed positive distance, proves a global C^(0,1/2) estimate for u_ρ. No logarithmic loss occurs.

Exact local products. For s=log r², the slope of F just inside r_j is B_j=Σ_{i>j}a_i=q₀a_j/(1-q₀), and just outside it is C_j=Σ_{i≥j}a_i=a_j/(1-q₀). Formula (4) in n5 gives EVERY lower product (DF)^l, with these B_j,C_j and c(r); for l=n the continuous term vanishes. Its sphere coefficient is
C_j^n-B_j^n=a_j^n(1-q₀^n)/(1-q₀)^n
           =A^n a_j^n/S_n.
Thus on B_{R_*},
(DF)^n=A^n S_n^(-1)Σ a_j^nσ_j=A^nρ.                        (9)
The shrinking-inner-truncation proof in n5 rules out any extra product at p and proves all lower products are locally finite.

Because χ=1 there, the complete bounded smooth-background corrected product is
MA_h(u_ρ)|_{B_{R_*}}=
 Σ_{l=0}^n binom(n,l)ε^l h^(n-l)∧(DF)^l.                  (10)
Each factor in each term is positive locally. Combining (4), (5) and (10) specifies the ordinary form parts and all spherical current parts; no unlisted negative correction or mass at p is present. On X\B_{R_*}, G=Aχ log r² is smooth, so the product is the ordinary smooth top power (h+εA D(χ log r²))^n. These expressions agree on the overlap. The l=n term in (10) and (9) imply globally MA_h(u_ρ)≥kρ. Entire mass is finite by the local traces in n5 and smoothness on the complement, and is at least k>0. Boundedness makes this the specified extended product as well.

A: probability, singularity and non-pluripolarity. The positive finite number S_n normalizes ρ to mass one. It is carried by the countable union of the smooth real hyperspheres, which has zero smooth-volume measure. Each σ_j is exactly the top product of the bounded continuous psh clipped logarithm in n5. The capacity argument in n1 therefore proves σ_j(P)=0 for EVERY locally pluripolar Borel P. Countable additivity yields ρ(P)=S_n^(-1)Σ a_j^nσ_j(P)=0. Each σ_j({p})=0, so ρ({p})=0 despite accumulation. This uses a countable sum, not any general weak-limit preservation assertion.

The construction depends on h, χ, the chart and the prescribed radii only; ν and λ do not enter it. Formula evidence is in checks/formulas_output.json: the symbolic sphere coefficient divided by A^n a_j^n/S_n is 1. Rerun python checks/verify_formulas.py. Full proof artifacts are notes/n5.txt and notes/n6.txt; computational checks corroborate algebra only.

notes.summary: C–D proved: every nonzero finite bounded measurable density against ρ has the common scaled subsolution and a separate exact normalized Hölder solution.
notes.detailedSummary: For M=Mρ(ν)<∞, 0<M<∞ and ν≤Mρ; hence ν is non-pluripolar and MA_h(uρ)≥(k/M)ν. This gives exactly the KN Hölder-subsolution hypothesis, yielding a new Hölder w with MA_h(w)=cν, c>0, sup w=0 and finite positive entire mass. Exactness comes from the theorem, not from dropping excess in the inequality. All bounded outputs belong to the stipulated E_env by its actual witness definition.
notes.text:
Assume 0<ν(X)<∞ and M=M_ρ(ν)<∞. By the definition in the question, ν=fρ with a measurable nonnegative density whose essential supremum is M. Choose a bounded Borel representative with 0≤f≤M everywhere after changes on a ρ-null Borel set. Since ρ(X)=1 and ν(X)>0, M≥ν(X)>0. Thus ν≤Mρ. Compact X is metrizable, so a finite Borel measure is Radon. By n6, ν(P)≤Mρ(P)=0 for each locally pluripolar Borel P. This proves non-pluripolarity even if it was not assumed initially.

C is immediate from the ACTUAL fixed potential:
MA_h(u_ρ)≥kρ≥(k/M)ν,   sup_X u_ρ=0.
Its finite positive mass and Hölder regularity are already proved in n6. There is no smooth-volume density truncation and no lower bound on f.

D is a distinct exact-equation application. We have
ν≤(M/k)MA_h(u_ρ),
where u_ρ is a global genuine C^(0,1/2) h-psh function. These are exactly the hypotheses of n2, with C₀=M/k. Consequently there exist genuine Hölder h-psh w₀ and c>0 with MA_h(w₀)=cν as measures. Set w=w₀-sup_X w₀. Compactness and continuity make this a finite subtraction, and Dw=Dw₀. Hence
sup_X w=0,    MA_ext,h(w)=MA_h(w)=cν,
0<MA_h(w)(X)=cν(X)<∞.
The product is the complete bounded corrected product from n5. No excess measure is removed from the subsolution; an exact equation is supplied by a separate primary theorem. Its Hölder exponent is some positive exponent, not asserted to equal 1/2. No optimal c, prescribed mass or homogeneous uniqueness is claimed.

Canonical values and the natural envelope class. Every bounded output b is a genuine quasi-psh function with finite values at every point. For the stipulated definition of E_env(X,h,0), fix t≥1 and take the constant genuine h-psh witness v_t=t inf_X b. Then t^(-1)v_t+(1-t^(-1))0=inf_X b≤b everywhere. Also b≼0 since b is bounded above. Thus u_ρ, w and every bounded exponential solution below lie in E_env by its actual witness definition. This does not replace that definition by unrestricted envelope equality.

Intrinsic meaning. For a FIXED global reference ρ, M_ρ is the measure-theoretic least domination bound and is independent of descriptions of that same measure. Different predetermined spherical reference measures can give different tests. Alternatively, existence of some holomorphic ball and radius system satisfying the explicitly stated measure condition is invariant under biholomorphic maps of manifolds: use the transported chart z∘T⁻¹, and transport the entire geometric configuration and its resulting measure. A new arbitrary chart need not reproduce the same spherical reference. This quantifies over explicit geometric data, not over potentials or solutions.

Proof and source artifacts are notes/n2.txt, notes/n6.txt and notes/n7.txt; rerun the source browser request for KN Definition 1.1/Theorem 1.3 from sources/requests.json, and python checks/verify_formulas.py for the reference algebra. No program purports to solve the exact PDE.

notes.summary: E proved by exact bounded-reference application: fixed ν and every λ>0 admit a unique bounded genuine exponential solution, without sup normalization or mass hypotheses.
notes.detailedSummary: Domination supplies ν=gMA_h(uρ), 0≤g≤M/k. The bounded reference uρ and the strictly positive big h meet ALS Theorem 5.1 exactly. Operator/background/measure rescaling leaves λ and the potential unchanged. The bounded-rooftop alternative handles compactness at v₋=0, and published bounded domination yields canonical pointwise uniqueness. Entire mass lies between e^(λinf U)ν(X) and e^(λsup U)ν(X).
notes.text:
Fix the SAME ν as in n7 and any specified λ>0. Let μ₀=MA_h(u_ρ). By n6 it is a finite positive non-pluripolar measure; by n7,
ν≤(M/k)μ₀.
The Radon–Nikodym theorem gives a bounded Borel g with ν=gμ₀ and 0≤g≤M/k everywhere after choosing its representative. This equality includes the smooth and spherical parts of μ₀; g is zero μ₀-a.e. on any excess part not charged by ν. The multiplier is genuinely bounded as a function on X. Its use is not a smooth-volume L∞ equivalence-class identification that discards its values on spheres.

Apply n3 with θ=h, ψ=u_ρ and this g. The genuine bigness hypothesis holds using the smooth potential 0, since h+D0=h≥h. The theorem permits g to vanish and requires only ν(X)>0. It supplies bounded genuine U_λ. Bounds initially expressed in L∞ hold at every canonical point: locally, the psh representative after adding a smooth quadratic is the limit of its ball averages, so essential bounds prohibit exceptional spikes or isolated poles. It satisfies the EXACT equation
MA_ext,h(U_λ)=MA_h(U_λ)=e^(λU_λ)ν.                           (11)
If the source operator is τD, apply it instead to θ_s=τh, ψ=u_ρ, μ_s=τ^nν=g MA_{θ_s,D_s}(ψ), with the SAME λ. Dividing its equation by τ^n gives (11) without an exponent or scalar error.

Compactness check at zero lower mass. The bounded-reference proof in the source uses uniformly bounded approximating solutions. For any such family x_j∈[-B,B], constants give
-B≤P_h(inf_j x_j)≤B.
This is a bounded genuine rooftop, and its class relative to the bounded reference 0 is E_env: for any t, a constant lower witness suffices, as in n7. Hence it is equivalent to 0. The local corrected-product estimate in n5 gives a uniform mass bound for this fixed B; no global v₊ is required. For the final density approximation, choose smooth nonnegative g_j with a uniform upper bound, strictly positive after adding a small constant, and converging in L¹(μ₀) to g. Such approximation exists for every finite Radon μ₀: approximate bounded Borel functions by continuous functions in L¹, clip in [0,M/k], then approximate continuously by smooth functions on compact X. The final source solutions have MA_h(x_j)≤Cμ₀ and are uniformly bounded. Its fixed-measure L¹ lemma gives
∫|e^(x_j)-e^x|MA_h(x_j)≤C∫|e^(x_j)-e^x|dμ₀→0.
Thus Lemma 4.3 uses its bounded-rooftop alternative, not v₋>0. Capacity convergence then passes the complete bounded product to the limit. The right side converges in total variation: for uniformly bounded x_j,
||g_j e^(λx_j)-g e^(λx)||_{L¹(μ₀)}
≤C||g_j-g||_{L¹(μ₀)}+C||x_j-x||_{L¹(μ₀)}→0.
This verifies the actual singular measurable-density passage rather than inferring product convergence from L¹ compactness alone. The source existence estimates themselves are invoked through Theorem 5.1.

Uniqueness is also independently checked from the published bounded domination principle in n4. Applying it to any two bounded solutions of (11), with shifts by δ>0 on strict-order sets and coefficient e^(-λδ)<1, proves equality everywhere in their genuine canonical representatives. This remains valid off supp ν.

Complete mass and normalization. Since U_λ is bounded,
0<e^(λinf_X U_λ)ν(X)≤MA_h(U_λ)(X)≤e^(λsup_X U_λ)ν(X)<∞.
The product agrees with the locally corrected bounded product in n5. There is no additional sup_X U_λ=0 normalization: adding t would multiply the right side by e^(λt) while leaving the left side unchanged. For the fixed ν and fixed scalar in (11), uniqueness makes this distinction mandatory. The natural class asserted is bounded genuine h-psh functions, a subclass of the stipulated E_env by n7.

notes.summary: Diagnostic proved: fixed Borel multipliers do not preserve weak MA convergence; smooth density approximation and a diagonal repair the relevant passage.
notes.detailedSummary: For smooth regularizations of a single clipped logarithm, the MA measures are absolutely continuous and converge to surface measure. Multiplication by the indicator of that sphere gives zero at every approximant but the full limit measure. A finite-Radon L¹ density approximation and weak-test-function diagonal avoid this error, preserving a uniform domination bound. This diagnosis does not refute the published exact theorem.
notes.text:
Observation in the primary evidence. The retrieved KN proof at printed p. 2958 introduces a Borel multiplier H of a reference Monge–Ampère measure and carries that same multiplier to smooth reference measures, asserting weak convergence. That inference is not valid for an arbitrary Borel H. The theorem statement is broader than a smooth-volume density assertion; this diagnostic prevents its proof shortcut from being used as an independent premise.

Explicit mathematical counterexample to the shortcut. In a coordinate ball let b=max(log|z|²,log r_j²). Its smooth decreasing psh regularizations b_m have absolutely continuous measures μ_m=(Db_m)^n, and n1/n5 give μ_m⇀σ_j. Let H=1_{|z|=r_j}. Then Hμ_m=0 for every m, since a sphere has zero Euclidean volume, but Hσ_j=σ_j≠0. Thus weak convergence of μ_m does not imply weak convergence of Hμ_m. This is a proof, not a numerical observation.

A valid density-diagonal construction. Let μ_m⇀μ₀ be finite positive measures on compact X and ν=gμ₀, with 0≤g≤K. Smooth nonnegative g_l with g_l≤K+1/l can be chosen so ||g_l-g||_{L¹(μ₀)}→0, by Radon regularity, continuous approximation, clipping and smooth approximation. For each FIXED l, continuity implies g_l μ_m⇀g_l μ₀. Choose a countable dense sequence of continuous test functions on X. Select m_l increasing so errors for the first l tests, and the constant test, are less than 1/l. Then g_l μ_{m_l}⇀gμ₀, with a uniform domination bound g_l μ_{m_l}≤(K+1)μ_{m_l}. The same diagonal can include g_l^(1/n), using |x^(1/n)-y^(1/n)|≤|x-y|^(1/n), so the strictly positive reference integral needed for a normalization estimate persists. At no stage is a Borel multiplier passed through weak convergence.

Actual smooth reference approximants exist for THIS construction. F in n6 is psh on a neighborhood of supp χ and is smooth on a fixed annulus outside all spheres. Convolve it locally with radial kernels, then set G_m=χ(F*κ_m), extended by zero, and normalize εG_m by its supremum. On χ=1 the convolved Hessian is positive. On the fixed annulus the functions converge in C², and εG had margin h/2. For sufficiently small kernels these smooth functions are genuine h-psh with margin at least h/3. They converge uniformly to u_ρ, with uniform C^(0,1/2) bounds. Closed local convergence plus smooth-background corrections gives μ_m=MA_h(u_m)⇀μ₀. Applying the density diagonal above therefore produces bona fide absolutely continuous approximating data for arbitrary bounded spherical densities.

This note proves the measure approximation repair only; it does not claim to reprove every uniform PDE estimate in the KN paper. D in n7 uses the stated published theorem. E in n8 uses a fixed reference μ₀ and the source's L¹(μ₀) density approximation, so it does not make this false multiplication inference. No failure of A–F follows from the diagnostic.
